rationale: The student focuses on individual digit size ('nines') instead of comparing from the greatest place value first. A place-value comparison model comparing two numbers where one has smaller leading digits but larger subsequent digits (e.g., 2,999 vs 3,001) reinforces starting at the thousands place.
intent: Demonstrate compare on the place-value with values [2999,3001]. Tutor points at: thousands place

frames.caption: Line up 2,999 and 3,001 by place. Start with the biggest place.
3 thousands is more than 2 thousands, so 3,001 is greater than 2,999. The smaller places cannot catch up, even if they are 9s.

judgement.reasoning: The demonstration directly addresses the exact misconception ('even if they are 9s, the smaller places cannot catch up') using an almost identical analog (2,999 vs 3,001) without leaking the exact problem (3,999 vs 4,001). It switches to a worked demo showing the comparison on a place-value grid highlighting the thousands place first.
judgement.verdict: Yes, this perfectly targets the misconception that 9s make a number bigger by showing that the thousands place decides the comparison.
